Scheme: not stated — actually the certificate is under scheme A or B? Not mentioned. The cert says "OIML Certificate of Conformity". R129-2000... Scheme not mentioned, so omit.

Issuing authority: NMi Certin B.V., Hugo de Grootplein 1, 3314 EG Dordrecht, The Netherlands. Person responsible: Ing. C. Oosterman, title: Manager Product Certification. Phone: +31 78 6332332. Email: certin@nmi.nl. Website: www.nmi.nl.

Applicant: SICK AG., Nimburger Strasse 11, D-79276 Reute, Germany.
Manufacturer: SICK AG., same address.

Certified type:
- Category: Multi-dimensional measuring instrument — hmm, the schema example categories: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter", ... This is a "Multi-dimensional measuring instrument" for measuring boxes (VMS 520 — volumetric measuring system). R129 is "Multidimensional measuring instruments". Category could be "Multi-dimensional measuring instrument" or "Measuring system". I'll use "Multi-dimensional measuring instrument".
- type_designations: ["VMS 520"]
- module_designation: Not applicable (this is a complete instrument; no modules named). Actually the description is given. I could set module_designation to null or "Not applicable". The cert doesn't mention modules, so null. Hmm, the schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Since no module mentioned, null is safe.
- description: "Multi-dimensional measuring instrument for measuring rectangular, non-rectangular, non-irregular shaped, non-reflective and opaque boxes."

Wait — "non-irregular" — that's what the text says: "measuring rectangular, non-rectangular, non-irregular shaped, non-reflective and opaque boxes." Actually that's odd but keep as written.

Model family: single model VMS 520, so no model_family needed (include ONLY if >1 model variant).

Table: dimensions L, W, H with Max ≤, Min ≥, d ≥:
- L: max 2000 mm, min 50 mm, d ≥ 5 mm
- W: max 1000 mm, min 50 mm, d ≥ 5 mm
- H: max 1600 mm, min 50 mm, d ≥ 5 mm
- Vmax ≤ 3 m/s

This is a configuration-axis matrix (dimension axis L/W/H). Could be captured via config_level with axis "dimension" and conditions L, W, H, and attributes max_length, min_length, graduation_interval... Or as matrix_tables.

Let me use characteristics.config_level:
- attribute: maximum_dimension, axis: "dimension (L/W/H)", values: [{condition: "L", value: {min:null,max:2000}, unit_symbol:"mm"}, {condition:"W", value: {min:null,max:1000}, unit_symbol:"mm"}, {condition:"H", value: {min:null,max:1600}, unit_symbol:"mm"}]

Hmm — the config_level value shape: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. Rule 5 says values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. So structured value objects with condition.

Alternatively use matrix_tables:
- name: "Measuring range by dimension", columns: ["dimension", "max", "min", "d"], rows: [{"dimension":"L","max":2000,"min":50,"d":5}, ...]

I'll do both: matrix_tables preserving the table, and config_level entries for max/min/d per dimension. Actually to avoid duplication, maybe just config_level. But rule says extract matrix tables AND populate model_level for R137. Here it's a config axis (L/W/H), so config_level. I'll also include matrix_tables for the raw table preservation. Hmm, the schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. Since config_level fits, maybe skip matrix_tables. But including it is safe and informative. I'll include config_level and skip matrix_tables to avoid redundancy? The instruction 5 for config axes: use config_level. I'll do config_level only, but maybe include matrix table too — the guidance "AND populate" for R137 example suggests populating both. I'll include both matrix_tables and config_level.

Actually, for consistency with the R137 example (which populates both matrix_tables and model_level), I'll include both matrix_tables and config_level here.

Also Vmax ≤ 3 m/s: transport speed. attribute: maximum_conveyor_speed or maximum_transport_speed, value {min:null, max:3}, unit "m/s". Type-level.

Maximum objects processed: 2400 per minute → attribute: maximum_objects_processed, value 2400, unit "per minute" or "1/min". I'll use unit_symbol "per minute". Hmm, maybe "objects/min". The text: "Maximum objects processed: 2400 per minute". value 2400, unit_symbol "per minute". Or unit_id null.

Temperature range -10 °C / +40 °C → value {min:-10, max:40}, unit "°C".

Recommendation: R129, edition 2000. amendment: null. scheme: not stated — omit. accuracy_classes: not stated.

Test reports: N° R129/2000-NL1-07.01, 64 pages, role: type_evaluation_report. Also mentions "EC-type-examination certificate and the description with number T10019 and the appertaining documentation folder" — T10019 is a description number. Could add test_reports entry: id "T10019", role "documentation_file"? It says "the EC-type-examination certificate and the description with number T10019 and the appertaining documentation folder" — these are referenced documents. Hmm, the description T10019 is part of referenced documentation. I could include it as documentation_file. But careful not to fabricate. The text clearly references "the description with number T10019". I'll include it as a test_report with role documentation_file... Actually the roles allowed: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. The description T10019 fits "documentation_file". I'll include it.

Revision history: none.

Footnotes: none.

- number: "R129/2000-NL1-07.01"
- scheme: not stated — omit or null. Rule 8: omit if not present. I'll omit.

- maximum_conveyor_speed: 3 m/s (Vmax ≤ 3 m/s)
- maximum_objects_processed: 2400 per minute
- temperature_range: {min:-10, max:40} °C

Config_level:
- attribute: maximum_dimension (max), axis "measured dimension", values L 2000mm, W 1000mm, H 1600mm
- attribute: minimum_dimension, values L 50, W 50, H 50 mm
- attribute: graduation_interval (d) — d ≥ 5 mm. In dimensioning of measuring instruments, d is scale interval. attribute: scale_interval? For R129 multidimensional instruments, d is the dimension division. I'll call it "dimension_division" or "graduation_interval_d". Rule 1 examples use snake_case. I'll use "scale_interval_d" ... Hmm. The table row "d ≥ 5 mm" — I'll name attribute "scale_interval" with footnote none. Let me use "scale_interval_d" to be safe? Canonical labels examples: maximum_capacity, max_load_cell_intervals_nlc, ratio_y_emax_over_vmin, apportionment_factor_plc. They keep suffix markers like _nlc, _plc. So "scale_interval_d" is fine. Values {min:5, max:null} since d ≥ 5. unit mm.

Matrix table:
{
  "name": "Measuring range by dimension",
  "columns": ["dimension", "maximum", "minimum", "scale_interval_d"],
  "column_units": [null, "mm", "mm", "mm"],

Hmm, for matrix table rows, maybe simpler numeric values. In the R137 example, rows had plain numbers with column_units. For max/min ranges, keeping structured range objects seems fine but simpler: "maximum": 2000 with the constraint implied. The R137 example rows use plain numbers. I'll use plain numbers in rows and note constraints in description, or keep structured. I think plain numbers with column_units is cleaner and matches example. The constraints Max ≤ / Min ≥ / d ≥ can be captured in description. Actually the schema for matrix_tables doesn't specify structured values for cells. The example used plain numbers. I'll use plain numbers and a description noting "Max ≤", "Min ≥", "d ≥".

Config_level values shape per rule 5: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. So:

{
  "attribute": "maximum_dimension",
  "axis": "measured dimension",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "L (length)", "value": {"min": null, "max": 2000}, "unit_symbol": "mm"},
    {"condition": "W (width)", "value": {"min": null, "max": 1000}, "unit_symbol": "mm"},
    {"condition": "H (height)", "value": {"min": null, "max": 1600}, "unit_symbol": "mm"}
  ]

Hmm, condition should just be "L", "W", "H".

minimum_dimension similarly with {min:50, max:null}.

scale_interval_d with {min:5, max:null}.
